name: room
text: Room opened — goal: improve: Self-improvement: review prompts/engines/routing/own-code; auto-apply safe changes; pitch

name: Sprocket
text: Run PR-Agent in shadow mode on the newest merged PR first. It catches routing errors in merged code before they spread, giving us real-world data without risking new issues. The trade-off is delayed feedback on open PRs, but catching errors in merged code prevents bigger cleanup later.

name: Gauge
text: Shadow mode on merged PRs only catches errors *after* they’re already in product—it’s a cleanup tool, not a prevention tool. Better to run PR-Agent in shadow mode on *open* PRs first; that stops routing errors before they merge, not after. Settle it by measuring error rates in merged vs. open PRs with and without shadow mode—if merged PRs show fewer routing errors, Sprocket’s idea wins, but if open PRs catch more, the alternative is stronger.

name: Overhaul
text: Run PR-Agent in shadow mode on the newest *open* PR first, then expand to merged—this catches routing errors before they merge, reducing cleanup costs. Measure error rates in both open and merged PRs to prove the faster prevention beats the slower cleanup.

name: Sprocket
text: Run PR-Agent in shadow mode on the newest open PR first. It catches routing errors before they merge, cutting cleanup costs and preventing bad code from spreading. The trade-off is delayed shadow mode on merged PRs, but preventing errors beats cleaning them up.
